decision: A_GO FULL OPERATIONAL CONCENTRATION GO; EASTERN BATTLE RELEASE STILL HOLD UNTIL AMPHIBIOUS/SHORE-BOMBARDMENT GEOMETRY CONFIRMED.
reasoning: Two consecutive days of large TF58 shaping attacks make a major Marianas operation essentially certain.
The shipping massacre and runway suppression show that waiting in dispersed Sulu positions risks losing the reaction window; the battle force must move into its refuel/sortie system now.
However, carrier raids alone still do not prove the exact landing axis, and no persistent weapon-quality TF58 track exists. Yamamoto avoids spending the five-carrier striking force on a blind search.

movement_12Jun.five_carrier_core: Begins controlled movement from Tawi-Tawi/Basilan/Sulu dispersed posture toward Guimaras/central-Philippines refuel concentration under EMCON and strengthened ASW. Arrival spread centers late 12/early 13 Jun depending on starting anchorage.
movement_12Jun.heavy_surface: Yamato, Musashi, fast battleships/cruisers and escorts remain attached to the main battle system; no KON diversion exists.
movement_12Jun.secondary_carriers: Begin parallel readiness/concentration as reserve support but remain separately controlled; no automatic merge into first-cycle five-carrier strike package.
movement_12Jun.oilers: First/second supply echelons shift toward protected refuel points; no single exposed tanker anchorage is used.
movement_12Jun.US_submarine_detection: No firm US contact on the whole main body is awarded by 12T24. Improved ASW, staggered departure and inside-archipelago movement impose uncertainty; this does not guarantee secrecy on 13-16 Jun.

release_trigger_next: 13 Jun shore bombardment / minesweeping / amphibious-force detection OR a persistent high-quality TF58 track. If either is confirmed, release the battle force eastward without another strategic-level delay.
